drafted_from: workflow:tell-the-owner-what-changed-for-each-person's own file (tools/workflows/recipes/tell-the-owner-what-changed-for-each-person.json) and its runs in the change-chain proof: six cases (a booking, a reschedule, a cancel, a rebook from a second address, a call under two hours away, a duplicate tell) on PGlite with stand-in tools.
start_here: Say to your AI: "Tell me when someone's bookings change, with a message ready to send." The AI switches on this workflow's wake every-five-minutes with your own settings; every five minutes your history says who has new settled changes, and you get one notice for each, a call to make now, or a draft waiting in your mailbox that you send yourself.
no_lists_because: It reads the person's own history (due_tells, history, known_as) and writes one tells row per notice there, in the person's own database; it keeps no list of its own.
instructions: 1. Keep changes in your history first (workflow:keep-each-told-change-in-the-history).
2. In your history, give each meaning that should reach you a tell_after (how long it settles) and tell_words for the sets of meanings told together; mark the schemes you are told about (told_about).

3. Switch on every-five-minutes with your own input: history, address_scheme, soon_minutes (a next call sooner than that is a call to make now), notices (credential_name: the vault name of the database your notices are kept in, the one workflow:read-my-notices reads; kind, needs-you when none), mail (provider, connection), calendar (provider, connection, calendar_id), voice (the scorer's draft-mode settings) and phrase_rules.
4. Each draft waits in your mailbox: sending it is your yes. Your sent-mail waiter tells the sent message back into your history as a sent statement, which has no tell_after, so it starts nothing.
5. Each notice is about one person, once: a second look at the same changes finds them told.

worked_examples.title: A cancel and a new booking from a second address are one notice that the call moved
worked_examples.ask: (the due-time noticer told this schedule is due)

worked_examples.hands_back: One tells row (person:bo, through statement 9, moved the call), one mail draft to the second address in the owner's mailbox, and one row of the owner's notices titled "A draft to <second address> is in your mailbox: moved the call" with its voice score and phrase findings.
